title: A gold camp that grew up overnight
text: In April 1895, Frederic Mooers, John Singleton, and Charles Burcham found gold at the Yellow Aster Mine, and a camp that became Randsburg grew around it. The mine and camp were named for the Rand, the gold mining region of South Africa. By the end of 1896, more than 1,500 people lived in the camp. As of 2020, Randsburg had 45 residents.
